resolutions.title: Concurrent writes can bypass the single-resolution rule
resolutions.resolution: Option A: a decision record is published by an exclusive temporary file and a link, so a same-token writer is refused instead of overwriting; the check-then-write race on the one-resolution rule is a named limit routed to stage parallel-lanes (R-adf-4), and the refusal names every resolution already naming the stop so a duplicate surfaces.
resolutions.action: composeDecisionRecord writes the temporary file with flag 'wx' and links it to the final name (never removing another writer's file); checkDecisionLinks names every resolution of the stop; orbit-decision-records' first requirement carries the named limit and residual; orbit-emit-composition's ADDED requirement states the no-overwrite publish with a scenario held by test/core/decision-records-race.test.ts; design Risks names it
resolutions.evidence: emit-composition.ts published via writeFileSync(tmp) + renameSync, and the sibling scan ran before it with nothing holding the folder

introduced.text: Named limit — the at-most-one-resolution check assumes one writer per `decisions/` folder at a time
#### Scenario: A same-token writer cannot replace a record

resolutions.title: Prototype property names bypass citation-kind validation
resolutions.action: a citation's kind is looked up by own property only, so an inherited key is refused like any unknown kind naming relies_on[i]; the same defect on the emit surface's command lookup (orbit emit toString passed the unknown-command check) fixed by commandSpec, an own-property read
resolutions.evidence: CITATION_SHAPES[c.kind] returned Object.prototype members; COMMANDS[command] likewise
